content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"Payments calls are running 34-44% above forecast since 12:00, and every call reason is up roughly 1.2-1.55x with no single reason dominating. AHT is at or below forecast, so this is not system slowness. Attendance is normal (2 sick vs 2 usual), and agents on phones are only 1-2 below plan, so this is not a sick wave. The only open incident is branch printers (branch-only impact), and the marketing calendar is empty. Demand has risen broadly with no identified driver. General is slightly elevated too, but its service level is 55-76%, below the 70% donor floor.","plan_name":"Payments surge recovery: borrow, buy and deflect","rationale":"Payments needs about 8-10 more agents to absorb roughly 35% extra volume. Moving staff from general is not allowed because its service level is under 70%. The free levers come first: delaying breaks in the 13:00-15:00 window and cancelling non-mandatory payments coaching for the afternoon. Overtime then adds sustained capacity: three consecutive 2-hour offers to 10 agents each, at about 40% acceptance, gives roughly 4 extra agents. That costs about Rs 8,640 if all three blocks fill, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Chat deflection at a 0.2 share of payment_status_enquiry and refund_status (about 45% of payments calls) removes about 9% of volume for little cost.
